beats.narr: This week's late-night snack: Jollibee fried chicken, sent to Donald Trump in Manila.
Trump did not say whether he had tried it.
The 'more popular than KFC' line rests on a readers' poll.

w261122b.end: The bucket has now beaten a president twice. Unopened.

beats.narr: On Monday a new James Bond was named. On Tuesday Jeff Bezos spoke.
He said he was "heavily involved" in the choice.
There were 5 finalists, with 3 scenes each.

w261122c.end: The jacket has been dry-cleaned. Pete has not.
w261122c.title: Pete is still in the tux
w261122c.claim: Jeff Bezos said on Tuesday he was "heavily involved" in choosing Robert Pattinson as the next James Bond, after screen tests of five finalists in full costume on real sets.
w261122c.why: Amazon bought MGM in 2022 and now controls Bond. Pattinson is the first 007 chosen without the Broccoli family, who had run the films since Dr. No in 1962.
facts: Bezos: he was "heavily involved"
5 finalists, 3 scenes each

Bezos: "it was so obvious he is James Bond"

beats.narr: Friday's summit: Britain and the EU agreed three deals in Brussels.
None starts until EU students pay what British students pay in fees.
Six months are set aside to settle the fees.
Lunch was cod and chips, then a Brussels waffle.

w261122d.end: Europe has six months. Rick has a third waffle.
w261122d.title: Rick is still digesting Europe
w261122d.claim: Prime Minister Andy Burnham and EU leaders agreed three deals at a summit in Brussels on Friday, on food and drink trade, emissions trading and a youth mobility scheme: the biggest step towards the EU since Brexit.
w261122d.why: Britain left the EU in 2020, after a 2016 vote. The EU says the three deals will not come into force until the UK gives EU students the fees British students pay.
facts: Three deals: food and drink, emissions, youth
Up to 100,000 under-30s each way, for 3 years
Burnham: +0.5% to GDP, a £17bn boost
EU: none in force without equal tuition fees

beats.narr: This week's word of the year was 'human'.
The dictionary says AI made people say it more.
It means having the faults and feelings people have.

w261122e.end: Gary stays human another week. Faults being counted.
w261122e.title: Gary is still human, on appeal
w261122e.claim: Cambridge Dictionary named 'human' its word of the year, saying the growth of AI means people now have to say 'human' for things that once only humans could do.
w261122e.why: The dictionary defines it as having the qualities, faults and feelings that people have, as opposed to gods, animals or machines. Compounds such as human-made are rising too.
facts: The word of the year: 'human'
Its use has grown four-fold since 1900
In English since the 14th century, from French
Rising too: 'human-made' and 'human-driven'
Chief editor: AI made it necessary to say it
